problems.stem: In repository Settings, under Pages, which Source setting publishes the site directly from your committed files?
options: Deploy from a branch, then choose main and / (root)
Upload a ZIP each time you change a file
problems.explanation: Choosing Deploy from a branch with main and the root folder tells GitHub Pages to build the live site from the files already committed on that branch.

problems.stem: Your page links the stylesheet as <link rel="stylesheet" href="/style.css"> and works locally, but on the published project site at username.github.io/portfolio the styles disappear. What is the fix?
options: Use a relative path like href="assets/style.css" (or include the /portfolio/ prefix) so the link resolves under the project subpath
Switch the whole site to a paid host
problems.explanation: A leading-slash path points at the domain root, not the /portfolio subpath, so the CSS 404s online. A relative path resolves correctly under the project site.

problems.stem: You push a change but the live page still shows the old version. An AI tool says 'the deploy is broken, recreate the repo.' Before doing anything drastic, what is the best check?
options: Recreate the repo immediately as the AI said
Hard-refresh the browser to clear the cache and check the Actions or Pages build status, since deploys take a minute and browsers cache
Push the same commit ten more times
Email GitHub support to reset your account
problems.explanation: Stale live pages are usually a build delay or a cached browser copy, not a broken repo. Verify the build finished and clear the cache before any destructive AI-suggested fix.

problems.stem: After publishing, what is the strongest evidence that your site actually works for a visitor, not just for you?
options: It looks fine in your own editor preview
You open the live username.github.io URL in a private window on another device and confirm every link and image loads
The commit succeeded with no error
A friend says the idea sounds good
problems.explanation: Local previews hide path and caching problems. Loading the live URL in a fresh private window on another device tests what a real visitor receives.
